scope: Private commercial projects; first-tier subcontractor contracting with the general (prime/original) contractor.
verification: CA, TX, FL, WA, AZ, NV checked 2026-10-25; CO, GA, IL, MN, NJ, NY, OH, PA, UT, VA checked 2026-11-08. Each against statute text quoted in search results from the official legislature domains below, or for GA (no per-section official site), CO (official code only as whole-title files) and NJ (no stable per-section link) from public copies of the code; full-page reads were not possible from the build sandbox. Needs a full read of each official page and attorney review before launch.

rules.title: Preliminary 20-day notice
rules.note: Serve the owner, the direct contractor and any construction lender within 20 days after you first furnish work. A late notice still protects work furnished in the 20 days before it is served, and after.

rules.title: Record mechanics lien
rules.note: The statute allows recording after you stop work and before the earlier of 90 days after completion of the whole project or 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. LienClock counts 90 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than completion. If a notice of completion is recorded, your real deadline can be earlier than shown.

rules.title: Notice of claim for unpaid work
rules.note: For each month in which you furnished labor or materials that are still unpaid, send notice to the owner and the original contractor by the 15th day of the third month after that month. A missed month loses lien rights for that month. Applies to original contracts dated on or after 2022-01-01. The statute moves a deadline that falls on a weekend or legal holiday to the next business day; LienClock shows the unextended date.

rules.title: File lien affidavit
rules.note: File with the county clerk by the 15th day of the fourth month after the month you last furnished labor or materials, and send a copy to the owner and original contractor. Retainage claims have their own deadlines (§ 53.057, § 53.052(d)) that LienClock does not track yet. Weekend and holiday deadlines roll forward under the statute; LienClock shows the unextended date.

rules.title: Notice to Owner
rules.note: Serve the owner (and the contractor) before you start or within 45 days after you start furnishing, and in any case before the owner makes final payment. A late or missing notice is a complete defense to your lien.

rules.title: Record claim of lien
rules.note: Record within 90 days after your final furnishing. If the original contract is terminated, the deadline is 90 days after termination when that is earlier.

rules.title: Record claim of lien
rules.note: Record within 90 days after you stop furnishing labor, materials or equipment, and give the owner a copy within 14 days of recording. A subcontractor contracting directly with the prime contractor on a commercial job needs no preliminary notice (RCW 60.04.031(2)(c)).

rules.title: Preliminary 20-day notice
rules.note: Serve within 20 days after you first furnish labor or materials. A late notice still protects work furnished in the 20 days before it is served, and after.

rules.title: Record mechanics lien
rules.note: The statute counts 120 days from completion of the whole project, or 60 days after a notice of completion is recorded. LienClock counts 120 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than completion. If a notice of completion is recorded, your real deadline can be earlier than shown.

rules.title: Notice of right to lien
rules.note: Deliver in person or by certified mail to the owner, with a copy to the prime contractor. It protects work furnished in the 31 days before it is given, and after, so give it within 31 days of first furnishing to cover everything.

rules.title: Record notice of lien
rules.note: The statute counts 90 days from the latest of project completion or your last work or delivery, or 40 days after a recorded notice of completion. LienClock counts from your last furnishing date, which is never later. Serve the owner within 30 days of recording.

rules.title: Notice of intent to file a lien statement
rules.note: Serve the owner (or reputed owner) and the prime contractor, in person or by registered or certified mail, at least 10 days before you file the lien statement, and file an affidavit of service with it. The lien statement is due 4 months after your last furnishing, so this is the last day to serve the notice and still file on time.

rules.title: Record lien statement
rules.note: File with the county clerk and recorder before 4 months after the day you last performed labor or furnished laborers or materials. If that month has no matching day, LienClock shows its last day. Colorado requires no preliminary notice from a subcontractor on a commercial job. Colorado publishes its code only as whole-title files, so this links to a public copy of the section.

rules.title: Record claim of lien
rules.note: Record with the clerk of the superior court within 90 days after you last furnished labor, services or materials, and mail the owner (and the contractor, if a notice of commencement was filed) a copy within 2 business days. Sue to enforce the lien within 365 days of recording. A subcontractor hired by the contractor needs no Notice to Contractor (§ 44-14-361.5). Georgia publishes its code without per-section links, so this links to a public copy.

rules.title: Subcontractor's 90-day notice to owner
rules.note: Within 90 days after you complete your work, give the owner (and the lender, if known) written notice of your claim and the amount due, by registered or certified mail with restricted delivery, or in person. Missing it can defeat your lien. The notice is excused if the GC's sworn statement lists you and the amount owed correctly, but don't rely on that.

rules.title: Record claim for lien
rules.note: Record your claim for lien with the county recorder within 4 months after you complete your work. A later claim can still bind the owner but not other creditors, lenders or buyers, so treat 4 months as the deadline. Illinois requires no preliminary notice on a commercial job.

rules.title: Prelien notice
rules.note: Give the owner the statutory prelien notice within 45 days after you first furnish labor, skill or materials; without it there is no lien. It is not required on a nonresidential project that adds more than 5,000 usable square feet, or on existing nonresidential property of more than 5,000 square feet (subd. 4c). If you aren't sure the exemption applies, give the notice.

rules.title: Record lien statement
rules.note: Within 120 days after you last furnished work, skill or materials, file the lien statement with the county recorder (or registrar of titles) and serve a copy on the owner in person or by certified mail. Both must happen within the 120 days.

rules.title: Lodge lien claim
rules.note: Lodge the lien claim with the county clerk within 90 days after the last date you provided work, services, materials or equipment (warranty and service calls don't count), then serve it on the owner and the GC within 10 days (N.J.S.A. 2A:44A-7). No preliminary notice is required on a commercial job. A bill pending in 2026 (A889) would lengthen the 90 days. The link is the 2010 law that set the current wording, because New Jersey's statute database has no stable per-section links.

rules.title: File notice of lien
rules.note: File with the county clerk within 8 months after the last item of work you performed or materials you furnished. Serve a copy on the owner within 5 days before or 30 days after filing, and file proof of service within 35 days of filing or the lien ends (§ 11). Serve the GC as well (§ 11-b). New York requires no preliminary notice on a private job.

rules.title: Notice of Furnishing
rules.note: Required once the owner has recorded a notice of commencement: serve the owner's designee named in it within 21 days after you first furnish. If the notice of commencement is recorded later, the 21 days run from then. A late notice still protects work furnished in the 21 days before it is served, and after.

rules.title: Record lien affidavit
rules.note: On a commercial job, file the affidavit with the county recorder within 75 days after the last day you performed labor or furnished materials, then serve a copy on the owner within 30 days of filing (§ 1311.07).

rules.title: Notice of Furnishing (projects of $1.5 million or more)
rules.note: Only on a project costing $1.5 million or more where the owner filed a Notice of Commencement in the State Construction Notices Directory: file a Notice of Furnishing in the Directory within 45 days after you first work at or deliver to the site. A subcontractor who doesn't comply forfeits the right to file a lien. If the project is smaller or has no Notice of Commencement, this deadline doesn't apply.

rules.title: Formal notice of intention to file a lien claim
rules.note: Give the owner formal written notice of your intention to file a claim at least 30 days before you file it, or the claim is invalid. The claim is due 6 months after you complete your work, so this is the last day to give the notice and still file on time.

rules.title: File mechanics' lien claim
rules.note: File with the prothonotary within 6 months after you complete your work (your last labor or delivery under your contract). Then serve notice of the filing on the owner within 1 month and file an affidavit of service within 20 days after that (§ 1502(a)(2)).

rules.title: Preliminary notice on the State Construction Registry
rules.note: File a preliminary notice on the State Construction Registry within 20 days after you start work. A late notice protects only work you provide from 5 days after it is filed, and none at all if it's filed more than 10 days after a notice of completion. Without one there is no lien.

rules.title: Record notice of lien
rules.note: The statute counts 180 days from final completion of the original (GC's) contract, or 90 days after a notice of completion is filed when that is earlier. LienClock counts 180 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than final completion. If a notice of completion is filed, your real deadline can be earlier than shown. Deliver a copy to the owner within 30 days of recording.

rules.title: Record memorandum of mechanics' lien
rules.note: The statute allows recording until 90 days after the last day of the month you last furnish, but never later than 90 days after the building is completed or work on it ends. LienClock counts 90 days from your last furnishing date, which is never later than either. As a subcontractor, also give the owner written notice of the amount and character of your claim (§ 43-7), and leave out work furnished more than 150 days before your last day on the job (retainage aside): including it can void the lien. Virginia requires no preliminary notice on a commercial job.
